name: AK-47
description: 7.62x39 assault rifle with a 30-round magazine. Reliable, with heavy recoil. Ammo for it is common.
about: Russian-pattern rifle, serial number ground off. They came in with the gangs before the collapse and have changed hands ever since.

name: Browning Hi-Power
description: Old 9 mm service pistol. A backup for when your rifle is empty.
about: The British Army's pistol until 2013. Thousands sat in stores until someone opened them.

name: Ka-Bar knife
description: Leather-handled fighting knife. Silent, with no ammo to run out of.
about: US Marine Corps issue. Whole crates went missing from the convoy depots.

name: K6-3 helmet
description: Heavy black helmet with a face visor. More protection than the MICH, at more than twice the weight.
about: Russian-made. Turns up wherever the AKs do.

name: MICH helmet
description: Modern combat helmet in a faded woodland cover. Lighter than the K6-3, no visor.
about: US Army issue. A name in marker inside the band: OKAFOR.

name: Plate carrier
description: Camo carrier with front and back plates and four magazine pouches. The heaviest item you'll wear, and the best protection.
about: US Army. PROPERTY OF US GOVT stencilled inside, half scrubbed off.

name: Chest rig
description: Tan X-harness rig. Keeps magazines and meds within quick reach.
about: A cheap copy of a NATO rig. They sold by the thousand online before the collapse.

name: Small assault pack
description: Small camo pack. Enough room for a short raid.
about: US Marine Corps. A unit patch has been cut off the flap.

name: Large rucksack
description: Large frame pack. Holds a lot of loot, but adds a lot of weight when full.
about: US Marine Corps, but someone carried it to the station: a council luggage label on the strap reads BLETCHLEY, GROUP B.

name: 7.62x39 FMJ (60)
description: Sixty full metal jacket rounds for the AK-47, in one grid square. The common type: good damage, and about half of it gets through armour.
about: Loose rounds from a box printed in Cyrillic.

name: 7.62x39 AP (60)
description: Sixty armour-piercing rounds. A little less damage than FMJ, but nearly all of it gets through armour.
about: Armour-piercing, black-tipped, picked out of a mixed tin by hand.

name: 7.62x39 hollow point (60)
description: Sixty hollow points. The hardest-hitting round, but armour stops most of it.
about: Hunting rounds from an Eastern European maker. Never meant for people.

name: Bandage
description: Heals 50 HP on a hurt body part that isn't bleeding or destroyed. Takes 3 seconds. One use.
about: British Army first field dressing. Every soldier carried two.

name: Surgical kit
description: Stops bleeding, or mends a destroyed body part. Three uses, 10 seconds each. The only thing that stops bleeding.
about: Field trauma kit from a military hospital store. The seal's been cut.

name: Painkillers
description: For 90 seconds: no head blur, hurt limbs work, and hits do a little less damage. They don't heal you.
about: Paracetamol, with an NHS pharmacy label for a Bletchley address.

name: First aid kit
description: A supply of 400 HP, shared out over hurt body parts at 3 seconds a part. Press H and the game picks what to treat.
about: NATO first aid pouch. The contents list is in English and Polish.

name: Tin of beans
description: A tin of baked beans. Keeps for years.

name: Sausage roll
description: Still in its paper bag, of uncertain age.

name: Bottle of water
description: Sealed bottled water. More valuable than it used to be.

name: Empty water bottle
description: What's left once the water's gone. Worth pennies.

name: Can of cider
description: Warm and flat, but still worth something.

name: Gold watch
description: A gold watch from someone's bedside drawer. High value for its weight.

name: Old smartphone
description: Dead and cracked. Worth something for its parts.

name: Concrete cow figurine
description: A miniature of Milton Keynes' concrete cows. Popular with collectors.

name: Old laptop
description: An old work laptop. Easy to sell, if you have room for it.

name: Copper wire
description: Stripped from the walls of the terraces. Always in demand.

name: Toolbox
description: Spanners, screwdrivers and a hammer. Useful, but heavy.

name: Car battery
description: Taken from a wrecked Corsa. Worth a fair amount, but it weighs 12 kg.
